notes:
I wasn't able to do this research, so I haven't written any verse notes for Ecclesiastes 5.

My first batch of page requests went over the tool's usage limit, and none of them came back. When I tried again with fewer pages, the tool refused because I had used up my allowed calls for this turn. I never read a single page. Your rules say to report only what the sources actually say, with a URL for each point, and not to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Any notes I wrote now would break those rules, so I've left everything out.

**What I would read when we try again:**
- **Traditional reading:** enduringword.com (Guzik on Ecclesiastes 5), preceptaustin.org's Ecclesiastes 5 commentary page, and biblehub.com's Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit Commentary and Wesley's Notes on chapter 5.
- **Differences between Protestant traditions:** Wesley's Notes on wesley.nnu.edu, plus targeted searches on ligonier.org, desiringgod.org, gty.org, 1517.org and lcms.org. The likely topics are worship and "the sacrifice of fools" (vv. 1–2), vows (vv. 4–6), and enjoying God's gifts (vv. 18–20).
- **Other views:** the netbible.org notes on the Hebrew (for example "messenger" in v. 6 and the hard-to-read vv. 8–9), and the Catholic and Orthodox sites. I'd also look for how the sites discuss prosperity teaching in light of vv. 10–20, and include it only if a site actually addresses it.

If you send the request again, I'll fetch fewer pages at a time so I stay under the limit. Or I can do it in parts, for example verses 1–7 first, then 8–17, then 18–20.
